items.title: Roger Kellaway interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999
items.q: After playing bass with Jimmy McPartland he moved to New York

ctx.x: Roger Kellaway has enjoyed a fruitful career in music as a pianist, composer and arranger. He was born in Newton, Massachusetts on November 1, 1939. He studied piano as a child and attended the New England Conservatory. After playing bass with Jimmy McPartland he moved to New York and played piano with numerous jazz artists, including Ben Webster, Clark Terry and Sonny Rollins. He re-settled in Los Angeles and performed with Don Ellis, Tom Scott and Joni Mitchell. Roger was Bobby Darin’s musical director in the…
Roger was interviewed in Los Angeles on February 14, 1999, by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.
